text: Based on previous work leading to a theoretical model of speech errors under DAF ( Malloy et al., 2022 ), we hypothesized that canonical DAF would cause more disruptive effects (larger changes in the dependent variables) compared to delayed EMN. Our hypothesis is based on the notion that the displaced rhythm associated with DAF (phase relationship between motor signals and auditory inputs) is responsible for feedback arriving during time windows of unexpected excitability within the auditory cortex, but that the content of the auditory input remains critical for triggering specific speech errors and increased interference during speech motor planning and execution. The results reported here constitute a test of the DRH, specifically focusing on the importance of the displaced rhythmic envelope, and provide strong counterevidence to the claim that asynchrony between the speech output signal and arriving auditory feedback signal is the sole driver of DAF-induced speech disruptions.
source_label: The effects of delayed auditory feedback depend on both the rhythm and content of the feedback signal
